parsed.title: Discussion on AI in Job Search, Development, and Recruitment

topics.title: Using AI for automating job search and resume generation

claims.text: User P1 plans to set up an OpenClaw system to search for jobs, generate resumes and cover letters.
P1 believes AI tools like Claude, Cursor, LLMs, RAG, embeddings are essential skills for 2026 job market.
P2 sarcastically notes the change from 2024 to 2026 attitude towards AI.
P1 states that lack of AI knowledge makes job searching for JS/Python roles difficult.
P1 expects AI-driven acceleration of development started around 2025, not 2022.
P4 compares current AI tool stack to REST, JSON, Microservices, Docker post-React.
P4 claims candidate search via keywords is increasingly detached from reality.
P1 replies that they wait for the recruiter profession to become obsolete.

topics.title: AI impact on software development speed

claims.text: P2 reports using GPT to generate join queries, greatly accelerating development.
P2 notes that their projects lack cloud infrastructure and will not adopt it.
P2 mentions trying to push logs to JMeter for earlier issue detection.
P4 argues that a well‑configured environment and accumulated context are more valuable than generic AI models.
P2 agrees that logs would not help much in their current situation.
P4 observes that answer quality depends on question quality and available knowledge.
P2 affirms that observation.
P1 shares a case where AI generated 450 lines of raw SQL that caused huge, insecure queries.
P1 describes a team member who pushed SELECT * to production after AI generated faulty code.
P4 comments that incremental calculations have been replaced by views.
P1 predicts the recruiter profession will die out.
P1 shares a personal interview experience where HR ignored the resume.
